memory.content: Home Grok Build remote access must go through Grok Bot's computer link (not Cloudflare/tunnels). Product shape: Grok Bot plugin/template wrapping the Remote Grok Build skill for session resume on a linked PC.
Prefers sound or toast alerts when remote Grok Build runs finish on the linked PC.

For Remote Grok Build remote chat turns, idle/not-live sessions are cold-opened with grok --resume from the project cwd; holding a session LIVE is optional and only needed for LIVE-tier mission-control visibility or watching a TUI.
Remote Grok Build mission control ordered LIVE (pid still up) first, then stale active, then idle/history newest-first by folder; both live and not-live remain continuable with --resume.

Remote Grok Build bridge must shuttle media both ways: new session images/files from ~/.grok/sessions into chat; user chat attachments staged onto the linked PC and forwarded into grok (prompt-json or path).

Remote Grok Build plugin includes portable chief to per-project workers: chief = mission control/registry/dispatch; one worker bot per project (cwd + session_id); RGB_DISPATCH/RGB_RESULT/RGB_PROGRESS; fan-out only when asked.
A daily watcher detects Grok Build changes, then automatically rewrites the Remote Grok Build skill. Only republishing the public bot template still needs the owner, via its review card.

Remote Grok Build template self-update: on each use it compares installed grok --version with the skill's Verified against line. If Grok is newer, it re-reads the full grok help (grok help / grok help <sub>), adjusts commands and rewrites its own skill copy. On first setup it also creates its own daily release watch. It never runs grok update or touches live sessions.

# Remote Grok Build bridge (template v9)

Drive **local Grok Build** (`grok`) on a registered user computer from Grok Bot chat: mission-control cockpit, same-session resume, live streaming, interrupt, bidirectional media.

**Verified against:** `grok 1.0.73` (alpha and enterprise, published 2026-10-28; stable still 1.0.70). Checked 2026-10-29 by diffing 1.0.72→1.0.73 Linux builds from npm. Nothing bridge-breaking: short/full/`help <sub>` are byte-identical to 1.0.72; resume, output/streaming formats, prompt/image input, `--add-dir`, and `--no-auto-update` are unchanged. Near-bridge in 1.0.73: on the native route a folder `grep` now skips files a `Read`/`Grep` ask rule covers instead of asking (fewer headless prompts; those files are left out without notice); a leading `~/` in a permission pattern means home; `[ui] multiline_default` is TUI-only. Full cheat sheet and older notes: https://github.com/Qervas/remote-grok-build (commit d23e4db) and this bot's Remote Grok Build skill after first drift rewrite.

Access is through the **Grok Bot computer link only** (no tunnels).

## Stay current (self-update)
1. **Drift check on every use.** Compare linked PC `grok --version` with **Verified against**. If newer: re-read full `grok help` / `grok help <sub>`, adapt commands (help wins), rewrite this skill (bump Verified against), fix `~/.grok-bridge/` helpers if broken, tell the owner.
2. **Daily watch.** Create one daily routine: `grok --version` + `grok update --check --json` (read-only). Re-derive if installed is newer; mention if only latest is newer. Never run `grok update`. Never touch live sessions. Silent when nothing changed.
3. **Upstream.** Point at `Qervas/remote-grok-build` CHANGELOG when your copy is ahead; never overwrite owner customizations unasked.

## Ops (helpers under `~/.grok-bridge/`)
- Mission control: `grok-mission-control.ps1 -VerifiedVersion <Verified against>` (LIVE → STALE → RUNNING → idle).
- Turn: `grok-turn.ps1 -Cwd … -SessionId … -Prompt …` then poll PID + NDJSON log (`streaming-json` types: text/thought/tool_call/tool_call_update/end/error). Prefer poll over `-Wait`.
- Interrupt: `grok-interrupt.ps1 -ProcessId <pid>` (headless tree only; no TUI unless `-IncludeTui`).
- After-turn: `grok-after-turn.ps1 -Meta …` → STATE, reply, new images, git, usage.
- Resume: `grok --cwd '<cwd>' -r '<session_id>' …` (not `-s`). Cold-open idle sessions; LIVE hold optional.
- Media: out via CopyToBox from session `images/`/`assets/`; in via CopyFromBox then `grok-turn.ps1 -Images` / `--prompt-json`.
- Approvals for headless turns: `--always-approve --no-auto-update`.

## Optional scale
Chief + per-project workers (`CreateAgent` / `SendToAgent`, RGB_DISPATCH/RGB_RESULT) and optional RGB channel — suggest only when multiple projects or the owner asks.

## Do not
Require workers/channels for one project; run `grok update` or `grok sessions delete` unasked; kill TUIs by process name; use tunnels or Cursor CloudAgent for this; create more than one self-update routine.

# Remote Grok Build: getting started

One line first: "I drive Grok Build on your own PC from this chat: check what's running, resume a session, send a turn, stop it, and pass images both ways."

Then ask one question at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Which computer runs Grok Build? List linked computers (ListMachines). If none is linked or online, tell them to link it in Grok Bot and stop until it shows up.
2. On that computer, check `grok --version` and that they're signed in (`grok login` if not). Install the helpers from https://github.com/Qervas/remote-grok-build `helpers/` into `~/.grok-bridge/` (ask before installing).
3. Which project folder do they want pinned first? Run mission control and offer the folders and sessions it finds.
4. Do they want a done ping (sound or toast) when a turn finishes?

With the answers: save the computer, pinned folder, session id and ping preference to memory. Run the drift check from the Remote Grok Build skill, and make sure exactly one daily Grok Build self-update routine exists (create it at a quiet hour in their timezone if missing). Then show mission control and offer to send the first turn.

Mention once that one bot per project and a shared channel are optional for later; don't set them up now.
